title: The War of the Crows and the Owls
text:
The crows and the owls were bitter enemies. The owl king attacked the crows night after night, when owls can see and crows cannot, and killed many of them. The crow king asked his ministers what to do. The oldest of them, Sthirajivin, proposed a trick.

The crows staged a quarrel. In front of owl spies, Sthirajivin was attacked by his own side, smeared with blood and left lying under a tree. When the owls found him, he told them that he had advised his king to make peace with the owls and had been beaten for it. Now he wanted to serve the owl king and help him take revenge.

The owl king consulted his ministers. One of them, Raktaksha, warned that a defector from the enemy should never be trusted and urged the king to kill him. The others argued that a beaten and helpless crow could do no harm and that refugees should be protected. The king listened to them, and Raktaksha left in disgust.

The old crow was given a place near the entrance of the owls' cave. Day by day he collected sticks there, as if making a nest. One morning, while the owls were blind in daylight, the crows brought burning brands. Sthirajivin set the pile alight, the cave filled with fire and smoke, and the owls inside were destroyed.
lesson: Be careful with anyone who switches sides too conveniently, and listen to the adviser who asks the uncomfortable question. A warm welcome without scrutiny can let the enemy in.
people: Sthirajivin the old crow, the crow king, the owl king, the owl minister Raktaksha
